title: Radical addition approaches for 2m/2π-intermolecular reactions of alkenes and alkynes
content: Selective radical coupling of two independent unsaturated molecules poses a distinct reaction-design problem: each π-component must be assigned a different role in the reaction sequence while homocoupling, oligomerisation and polymerisation are suppressed. This review introduces the 2m/2π framework, in which two molecular components and two reactive π-bonds are assembled into a discrete product, and uses it to organise intermolecular radical reactions of alkenes and alkynes. Rather than classifying transformations primarily by reagent or catalyst, we analyse the factors that differentiate the π-components: radical polarity matching, group-transfer events, direct redox resolution, bond multiplicity, reversible radical addition and metal-supported activation. Electrophilic-, nucleophilic- and metal-hydride-initiated ene–ene cascades are compared with group-transfer radical addition, redox-driven couplings and the less developed ene–yne and yne–ene manifolds. Particular attention is paid to the origins of chemo-, regio- and stereoselectivity, the termination pathways that prevent uncontrolled propagation and the substrate limitations of each strategy. The resulting framework connects previously separate reaction classes, identifies underexplored yne–yne and asymmetric coupling space, and provides practical design principles for selective multicomponent radical assembly.
